repository_purpose: Composable browser automation and UI testing stack that layers skills, subagents, commands, and just recipes for repeatable browser-driven validation.
findings: Bowser is not parent core by itself, but it is a strong browser-validation lane when promotion requires UI or browser evidence.
The four-layer stack is useful as a pattern for decomposing browser work, yet the parent only needs the governed lane and resulting evidence types, not the upstream folder mirror.
The upstream runtime is Claude-oriented and Playwright-dependent, so this lane should remain gated until the parent truly needs browser proof.

capability_rows.upstream_feature_name: browser automation and UI validation lane
capability_rows.validation_method: Validate that browser runs emit reproducible evidence (screenshots, DOM/output captures, or step logs) and that the promotion decision names why browser proof was required.
capability_rows.blocker_or_dependency: Gated on a real browser-validation requirement plus Playwright CLI or an equivalent browser control surface; otherwise the parent should not pretend this lane is active.

trigger_logic: Use only when a promotion or evaluation slice explicitly depends on browser-observed behavior.
actor_logic: The mesh verifier or QA browser worker owns the lane and the attached proof artifact.
validation_summary: Require machine-readable evidence of what the browser lane actually observed.

overlaps: Agent-sandbox-skill can host browser work inside an isolated environment, but Bowser itself does not provide isolation.
Mac Mini Agent covers GUI/device control at the OS layer rather than browser-specific validation.
blockers: No exact blocker if the lane is intentionally enabled, but there is no current parent requirement that makes it core.

source_refs.note: Documents the four-layer architecture, Claude/Playwright dependencies, and browser-test workflows.

github_verification.note: GitHub due diligence pinned the cited upstream files to the verified commit snapshot used for this packet.
